{"say":"A voice kit for Skerrow: oaths by the Tidemother and the Old Stars, sworn on sea, salt and tar, a few island sayings, and two groups. The hythe folk (fishers, boatmen, innkeeper) speak of tar and nets. The Heights folk (lightkeeper, hedge-witch, scholar, steward) speak of lamp and stone. Time is counted in tides and bells, distance in oar-strokes and cables, and the weekdays and months of our world are set aside for tide-days and storm-months. Every name comes from the world as it stands.","yaml":"voice:
  oaths:
    tidemother:
      - "Tidemother take me if I lie."
      - "By salt and tar and the Mother's grey hand!"
      - "What the tide gives, the tide takes."
    old_stars:
      - "By the Old Stars!"
      - "Stars keep us, and keep the rest of you too."
      - "Broken sky and burning tar!"
  sayings:
    - "Tar your hull before the storm, not in it."
    - "The sea keeps no ledger, but she never forgets a debt."
    - "A dark lamp is a hungry shore."
    - "Old Skarth sleeps; let him."
  groups:
    - id: hythe_folk
      name: the Hythe folk
      areas: [skerrow_hythe, skerrow_shore]
      professions: [fisher, boatman, innkeeper, child]
      sayings:
        - "Pitch in the seams, bread on the board."
        - "Mend the net while the fish are elsewhere."
        - "Nobody drowns in the Salt Kettle but by the tankard."
      oaths:
        - "Tar and tide!"
        - "Sink me for a leaky dory."
    - id: heights_folk
      name: the Heights folk
      areas: [skerrow_heights, skerrow]
      professions: [lightkeeper, hedge_witch, scholar, steward]
      sayings:
        - "Oil for the Lamp before bread for the keeper."
        - "Stone remembers what the sea forgets."
      oaths:
        - "By the Lamp of Skerrow!"
  default_group: hythe_folk
  address:
    stranger: ["stranger", "castaway", "you off the Gull"]
    known: ["neighbour", "shipmate"]
    friend: ["old salt", "my heart", "tar-hand"]
    high: ["master steward", "keeper", "goodwife", "goodman"]
  time:
    - "a tide (half a day)"
    - "a bell (an hour)"
    - "slack water"
    - "first bell, last bell"
    - "the turn of the tide"
  distance:
    - "a cable's length"
    - "a hundred oar-strokes"
    - "a shout off"
    - "a day's sail"
  measures:
    - "a fathom"
    - "a barrel of pitch"
    - "a creel of fish"
    - "a tankard"
  not_here:
    - word: minute
      instead: a breath, a short while
    - word: mile
      instead: a hundred oar-strokes
    - word: Monday
      instead: first tide-day
    - word: Sunday
      instead: Mother's day, the rest day
    - word: December
      instead: Storm-month
    - word: June
      instead: Long-light
    - word: okay
      instead: aye, fair enough
    - word: dollar
      instead: silver piece"}
